summary: Private deployment TLS rotation triggered control-plane failover and temporary routing to hosted runtime — potential data exposure for VeritySchools
description:
Issue summary:
On 2026-02-18 at ~08:12 UTC VeritySchools (private deployment, eu-west) reported repeated model responses containing content from other customer sessions. Initial triage showed a control-plane health check spike after the customer's scheduled TLS certificate rotation. The Redwood control plane marked several private nodes as unreachable and policy routing unexpectedly routed a subset of traffic to the hosted inference fleet for failover. That hosted path accepted requests for a short window before route restrictions were applied, resulting in transient telemetry and logs containing request/response fragments that belonged to VeritySchools sessions.

Impact:
- Customer-facing: Multiple VeritySchools sessions observed interleaved transcripts (4 distinct customers reported).
- Security: Potential exposure of session text to hosted runtime telemetry for up to 11 minutes. No confirmed permanent data persistence in hosted customer indexes; however audit logs contained request IDs and partial transcripts.
- Business: Customer classified incident as Major and paused production traffic; requested immediate remediation and evidence for compliance audit.

Timeline (high level):
- 08:10 UTC: VeritySchools rotates TLS cert on their LB per maintenance window.
- 08:12 UTC: Control plane health probes start failing for private nodes.
- 08:13–08:24 UTC: Automated routing policy starts failover; a subset of requests forwarded to hosted pool.
- 08:25 UTC: Support/SRE alerts on cross-session transcript reports from VeritySchools.
- 08:30 UTC: Controls tightened — routing blocked to hosted fleet for this customer; audit mode enabled.
- 09:05 UTC: Full rollback re-established to private nodes after coordination with customer; incident declared mitigated.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VeritySchools customer-managed nodes) behind customer LB.
- Redwood control plane in eu-west region.
- Affected model variants: redwood-1.3-std (default), openllama-13b-quant (fallback).

Steps to reproduce (reconstruction):
1) Simulate a control-plane health probe failure by returning 503 from private node health endpoint while leaving TLS termination path intact.
2) Observe routing policy: requests are rerouted to hosted fleet if node marked unhealthy and customer has failover policy enabled.
3) Confirm hosted fleet accepts requests and logs telemetry for request IDs before route filters apply.

Evidence collected:
- Control-plane health logs (cp-health-logs-2026-02-18T08-12.gz) showing probe failures.
- Routing decision traces (trace-ids: rtr-20260218-08-13-ae44).
- Audit log snippets showing partial transcripts and request IDs (stored in secure audit bucket).
- Customer screenshots and exported transcripts.

Immediate mitigation actions taken:
- 08:30 UTC: Emergency rule pushed to routing service to prevent any private-customer routing to hosted pool unless explicit manual override present.
- 08:34 UTC: Audit mode enabled to capture all hosted telemetry for investigation; retained artifacts moved to isolated S3 path with limited access.
- 09:05 UTC: Coordinated with VeritySchools to complete TLS rotation and validate private nodes; traffic resumed to private pool.

Current status and ask:
- Status: Resolved (private routing restored, hosted access blocked, audit artifacts secured).
- Customer requested written attestation and list of retained artifacts plus full post-incident remediation plan and timeline for an RCA.

Recommended immediate follow-ups (high level):
- Provide VeritySchools with an itemized audit export of affected request IDs and transcripts (redacted as necessary) and legal/ compliance statement.
- Implement a policy change: during customer-managed TLS rotations, treat transient probe failures as 'degraded' but do NOT auto-failover to hosted routes for private-tier customers unless explicitly allowed.
- Add control-plane safeguard: require authenticated reroute token for any cross-environment fallback.
comments: Support (Aisha): 2026-02-18 08:29 UTC - Customer reported 'mixed transcripts' and shared two transcript excerpts. Opened incident and paged SRE.

SRE (Miles): 2026-02-18 08:32 UTC - Observed control-plane health flapping for VeritySchools nodes. Initial hypothesis: customer-side TLS rotation caused health probe failures triggering failover logic.

Customer (VeritySchools - Elena Park): 2026-02-18 08:40 UTC - Confirmed TLS rotation started at 08:10. Expressed concern about data residency and asked for immediate confirmation of where requests were routed.
Support (Aisha): 2026-02-18 08:50 UTC - Notified customer that we are enabling audit capture and will block further hosted routing while investigating.
SRE (Miles): 2026-02-18 09:06 UTC - Restored routing back to private nodes after customer validated endpoints. Will collect and preserve artifacts for compliance.
Security (Nadia): 2026-02-18 10:12 UTC - Performed scoped review of hosted logs. Found transient telemetry for request IDs but no persistence to search indexes. Ongoing review with legal.
Support (Aisha): 2026-02-18 12:00 UTC - Shared temporary mitigation steps and apologized. Customer accepted interim measures, requested RCA and formal attestation by EOD.
SRE (Miles): 2026-02-22 14:32 UTC - Submitted internal change proposal to add TLS-rotation detection flag to control plane and block auto-failover for private customers (see linked PRs).
Customer (Elena Park): 2026-02-23 09:00 UTC - Received formal attestation and accepted remediation plan. Confirmed re-enabling of production traffic.
investigation_notes: Checked control-plane health metrics: spike of probe failures at 08:11-08:14 UTC correlated exactly with customer's rotation window.
Routing logic: current failover policy treats node 'unhealthy' as trigger to route to hosted pool when available. No additional guard for 'private' customers was present.

Audit logs: hosted telemetry contained request IDs and partial payloads for 37 requests over 11 minutes. Payloads matched VeritySchools session IDs; full transcripts were not indexed but were present in ephemeral logs stored in telemetry pipelines.

Security review: no evidence of exfiltration beyond ephemeral telemetry. We rotated access keys to telemetry store and revoked prior temporary tokens for review access. Legal engagement opened for compliance attestation.

Hypothesis: customer-managed TLS rotation caused health-check TLS handshake failures; control plane marked nodes unhealthy based solely on health probe responses. Because of a permissive failover policy, routing sent traffic to hosted fleet before route restrictions applied.
resolution: Mitigation and fix rolled out: 1) Immediate: blocked hosted fallback for all private customers by default and enabled audit-only capture for the affected window; provided VeritySchools with an export of affected request IDs and redacted transcripts. 2) Short term: deployed control-plane change to treat repeated probe failures during customer-initiated TLS rotations as 'degraded' instead of 'unhealthy' for 7-day canary. 3) Medium term: implemented an authenticated reroute token requirement and added a TLS-rotation detection flag in control-plane API; corresponding routing PRs merged (see related_github_prs). 4) Follow-ups: schedule a joint runbook review with VeritySchools to coordinate future rotations; SRE to update runbook and add tests to simulate TLS rotation. Post-incident action items assigned: INT-33045 (implement guard), INT-33046 (audit export delivery), INT-33047 (runbook update). Incident closed on 2026-02-23 after customer acceptance.
